title: Utility of the use of N-acetylcisteine associated with conventional treatment in patients with severe acute alcoholic hepatitis (Maddrey>=32)
official: Utility of the use of N-acetylcysteine associated with conventional treatment in patients with severe acute alcoholic hepatitis (Maddrey>=32)
summary: Main objective: To assess the efficacy of the use of methylprednisolone + NAC, in terms of 1 month mortality, in patients with Severe Alcoholic Hepatitis
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Males and females
2. Age from 18 to 75 years.
3. Diagnosed with acute alcoholic hepatitis per AASLD guidelines or compatible liver histology
4. Maddret Score >= 32
5. Willingness to participate expressed through written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
1. Alternate cause of jaundice
2. Uncontrolled concomitan diseases (HBV, HCV, HIV, TB, DILI, HCC or acute pancreatitis)
3. Multiple organ failure or shock
4. Allergy or intolerance to NAC and/or corticosteroids
5. Hepatocellular carcinoma
6. Pregnancy
7. Life expectancy under 12 months due to comorbid conditions
8. Current treatment with nitroglycerin and/or carmazepine
9. Uncontrolled active infections
10. Acute renal failure with creatinine > 2,5 mg/dL
11. Uncontrolled upper gastrointestinal bleeding
sponsor: Asociacion Instituto De Investigacion Sanitaria Bioaraba
